submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires when the current token opens or heads a new finite clause in narrative or quoted discourse: a complementizer or relativizer (that/which), a clause-initial past auxiliary or modal (was/Would/Could), or the finite predicate or subject head of the clause (content/died/possible/wollte/quoth), with most strength when licensed by a long-range cue such as a cognition or speech verb, negation, or sentence-boundary punctuation. The same surface token placed NP-internally (determiner that, non-clausal nominal) or the same modal embedded mid-sentence without a boundary licensor drives it weakly.

2. Originally Posted by bhuang

b^(log of x to the base b) = x

I don't even know solve for this myself. Could someone please show their work for this?
Given that $b,c \neq 0,1$ and $x > 0$ so the domain is satisfied

Suppose the following is true: $b^{log_b(x)} = x$

Take the log of both sides

$log_b(x)log_c(b) = log_c(x)$

From the change of base rule $log_b(x) = \frac{log_c(x)}{log_c(b)}$

$\frac{log_c(x)}{log_c(b)} \, log_c(b) = log_c(x)$

$log_c(b)$ cancels to give $log_c(x)=log_c(x)$

Therefore it is true.

3. $a^b=x,\ log_ax=b$

You can think of it as just "sliding" the "a" over to the underside of x,
or vice versa.

$y=b^{log_b(x)}$

$log_by=log_bx$

$y=x$

- Watani walisema gavana wa Mombasa alikuwa amepata namna ya kufukuza kibaridi kikali kinachoshuhudiwa kwa kusisimua misuli pamoja na Waiguru
- Joho alisema walikutana ili kujadili maslahi mazito ya taifa wakati wa kikao chao
Magavana Ann Waiguru wa Kirinyaga na mwenzake wa Mombasa Hassan Ali Joho Jumatano Julai 14 walichemsha mtandao baada ya kuonekana wakijivinjari.
Picha za wawili hao wakiwa uwanjani kucheza gofu zilipakiwa mtandaoni na mara moja zikawa kama moto unaoshika kichaka kikavu.
Wawili hao walionekana katika manthari ya kuvutia ambapo walikuwa wameenda kusisimua misuli kwa kucheza gofu.
Huku wakiwa wamevalia kispoti na kwa namna ya kuvutia, picha moja iliwanasa kwenye mwendo wa aste.
Joho huwa ni mmoja wa viongozi tanashati ambaye huwavutia vipusa kama vile ua nzuri kwa kipepepo huku Waiguru naye akiwa na uso mtamu kiasi cha kuwakosesha mafisi usingizi.
Licha ya kuwa miaka ya wawili hao imesonga, wangali wanaonekana wakivutia mno huku mavazi yakibana miili yao.
Joho alikuwa wa kwanza kuchapisha picha hizo kwenye ukurasa wake wa Twitter akisema walikutana kujadili masuala mazito.
Baadhi ya wanamtandao waligeuka watani na kusema Joho aliamua kukabili msimu huu wa baridi kwa namna spesheli.
Silvia Wangeci alichapisha kwenye twitter picha aliyodai ni ya mpenziwe Waiguru akichoma mahindi kumaliza baridi huku naye Joho akipiga tizi na gavana huyo wa Kirinyaga.
Mwanamtandao Heisenberg alisema kwake yeye picha zilitoa uhondo wa kutosha na hivyo hakuna haja ya kusema mengi.
"Ilikuwa furaha kukutana na gavana mwenzangu wa Kirinyaga Anne Waiguru leo alasiri kucheza gofu. Tulipata muda pia wa kujadili masuala ya maslahi ya kitaifa," alisema kwenye twitter yake.

Are you a middle or high school teacher seeking support for discussing slavery with your students? Providing an inclusive classroom environment and building empathy requires teaching a history curriculum that reflects the diversity of the present and engages with the tough questions of the past. This seminar will introduce resources to teach American slavery across the chronology and geography of American history, allowing attendees to envision and teach slavery as fundamental, and not incidental, to the history of the United States. During this workshop, teachers will work with a selection of resources and teaching strategies.
Understanding and Teaching American Slavery, co-edited by Dr. Bethany Jay, won the 2018 James Harvey Robinson Prize “for the teaching aid that has made the most outstanding contribution to the teaching and learning of history in any field for public or educational purposes.” It will be available for purchase before the workshop.
Workshop is open to the public, with a focus on engaging educators of middle and high school students. Registration required no later than one week in advance. Co-sponsored by the Connecticut Council for the Social Studies.
Bethany Jay is an associate professor of history at Salem State University. She earned her Ph.D. from Boston College in 2009 and teaches courses in nineteenth-century American history, public history, and history education.
